jobs.description:
仿真场景搭建与资产配置:基于 NVIDIA Isaac Sim、Newton(Palatial/MuJoCo)等仿真平台,负责数字孪生场景搭建、机器人(如双臂机械臂、复合移动机器人)及物体的物理/渲染属性(USD、MJCF、Mass、Inertia、Bounds、CoACD 碰撞分解)配置与优化。
 抓取与操纵逻辑开发:负责物体抓取(Grasp Pose)、逆运动学(IK)、接触物理(Contact/Friction/Restitution)以及状态机(State Machine)逻辑的编写与测试。
 行为脚本与任务规划:编写基于 Python 的自动化行为脚本(Harness/Task Pipeline),实现“接近-抓取-抬起-振动/扰动测试-放置”等复杂离散/连续行为动作的逻辑控制与闭环校验。
 验证与指标分析:构建仿真测评 Pipeline(Metrics System),输出抓取成功率、滑移量(Contact Slide)、接触力等评估数据,并基于测试结果反向迭代 IK 与 Grasp 参数。
 算法协同与交付:与具身智能(Embodied AI)算法团队合作,为强化学习(RL)、模仿学习(Imitation Learning)或大模型部署提供高保真、稳定高并发的仿真环境与数据集生成接口。
 Real2Sim 与 Demo 生成:将第一人称视角(egocentric)等各类数据转化为高质量的 real2sim2real 仿真,用于数据集生成与 Demo 制作。
requirements: 计算机、机器人学、自动化、机电一体化等相关专业,本科及以上学历。
1 年及以上具身智能(Embodied AI)、机械臂抓取操纵或机器人仿真相关行业工作经验。
项目经验须体现机械臂抓取、灵巧手或接触操纵(manipulation)方向;仅有导航/SLAM/无人机/自动驾驶仿真经验、无操作类项目者不匹配。
精通 NVIDIA Isaac Sim (Omniverse) 或 Newton / MuJoCo 仿真框架,熟悉 USD / MJCF 物理描述文件结构。
熟悉仿真物理引擎机制(刚体动力学、接触力学、碰撞网格分解、CCD等)。
精通 Python,具备扎实的数据结构与软件工程规范,能够熟练编写面向对象的复杂逻辑脚本与自动化框架。
熟悉机器人学基础(空间变换、正/逆运动学 IK、碰撞检测算法)。
熟悉 Linux 深度开发环境、Git 版本控制与虚拟环境管理(venv / conda)。
具备严谨的调试与测试思维,能够独立追踪解决物理穿透、发散、接触抖动等仿真异常现象。
5. 英语能口头与书面沟通,能阅读英文技术文档
有 Palatial Newton、Isaac Gym 或 Brax 等高性能/并行仿真器实际项目经验者优先。
熟悉 ROS / ROS 2,具备硬件真机(如 UR、Franka、Yam 机械臂)部署或仿真到真机(Sim2Real)经验者优先。
熟悉 OpenCV、合成数据生成(SDG / Replicator)或 PBR 渲染(RTX 光线追踪、光源与材质优化)者优先。

jobs.title: 海康机器人-伺服算法工程师-工控-杭州招聘_海康威视招聘 - 智联招聘
jobs.description:
职位描述: 
1、熟悉伺服产品应用场景,专注通用伺服驱动器控制算法研究和迭代。 
2、具备丰富的量产伺服产品算法调试、问题攻坚、性能优化实战经验,能够独立发现产品控制短板,输出优化方案并落地验证,持续提升伺服产品响应速度、控制精度及工况适配性,支持产品差异化竞争与高端化升级。 
3、负责伺服三环(位置环、速度环、电流)控制算法优化,针对超调、震荡、低速抖动、高速响应滞后、稳态误差大、负载适应性差等都有切实的落地改良方案。 
4、对参数自辨识、死区补偿、摩擦力补偿、间隙补偿、高频振动抑制、低频抖动消除、弱磁控制、抗负责扰动观测、自适应PID、前馈控制等高性能算法都有深刻的理解,并能独立完成设计、仿真、代码实现及整机调试。 
5、跟踪先进伺服控制技术,结合公司产品定位,将新技术转化为量产可用方案,推动产品性能迭代升级。 
任职资格: 
1、硕士及以上学历,3年以上伺服(永磁同步电机)控制算法开发经验。 
2、有伺服三环(位置、速度、电流)控制算法优化落地应用经验,对伺服常见问题如速度超调/震荡、低速抖动、响应滞后、鲁棒性差等有优化经验。 
3、具备丰富的量产伺服产品算法调试、问题攻坚、性能优化实战经验,能够独立发现产品控制短板,输出优化方案并落地验证,持续提升伺服产品跟踪精度和鲁棒性,支持产品差异化竞争与高端化升级。 
4、对伺服速度控制高性能算法如机械/电气参数辨识、扰动观测器、摩擦力补偿、间隙补偿、振动抑制(高频共振和末端残余振动)、PID参数自适应等有实际开发经验,能独立完成算法设计、仿真设计、代码实现和调试闭环。 
5、对伺服电流控制高性能算法如弱磁控制、MTPA、模型预测控制、电流解耦等高性能算法有深刻的理解,并能独立完成算法设计、仿真、代码实现及整机调试。 
6、有伺服驱动器产品量产化应用经验优先。 
7、具有较强的软件调试能力,具备一定抗压能力。

jobs.description:
人工智能工业自动化/机器人
岗位职责: 
1、负责通用多模态大模型、VLA、世界动作模型等在人形机器人/机械臂真实场景中的算法设计、研发与部署,面向机器人操作、人机交互等任务构建端到端感知、理解与动作生成能力。 
2、负责真实机器人平台上的训练数据集构建,涵盖视觉、语言、动作轨迹等多模态数据,支撑多模态大模型参数调优。 
3、研究并开发面向真实机器人操作任务的模仿学习、真机强化学习等方法,提升机器人在复杂任务中的泛化能力、鲁棒性和连续多步骤执行能力。 
4、推进VLA模型、世界动作模型与机器人控制系统的结合,实现从任务理解、动作预测、轨迹生成到真机执行的闭环优化。 
5、基于ROS/ROS2等机器人系统框架完成算法集成、部署调试与实验验证,可结合Isaac Sim、MuJoCo等仿真平台进行算法预验证和辅助分析。 
6、跟踪多模态大模型、VLA、强化学习、世界动作模型等方向的前沿进展,探索其在真实机器人操作场景中的落地路径。
requirements: 1、计算机、人工智能、自动化、机器人等相关专业,硕士及以上学历优先。
2、具备扎实的深度学习和多模态模型基础,熟悉Transformer、ViT、VLM、VLA、Diffusion等主流模型架构,有大模型训练、微调、推理优化经验者优先。
3、熟悉机器人学习相关方法,包括模仿学习、强化学习、轨迹预测、动作生成、策略优化等,有真实机器人数据采集和训练经验者优先。
3、具备机器人系统开发基础,熟悉ROS/ROS2、机器人运动学、轨迹规划、控制接口、传感器数据处理等,有机械臂、人形机器人或灵巧手真机开发经验者优先。
4、熟练使用PyTorch、TensorFlow等深度学习框架,具备良好的算法复现、模型训练、实验分析和工程实现能力。
5、熟悉具身智能相关开源框架、数据集或模型者优先,如OpenVLA、ACT、Diffusion Policy、π0、GR00T、LeRobot等。
6、具备良好的问题分析、工程调试、团队协作和沟通能力,能够围绕真实机器人任务持续迭代算法效果。

jobs.description:
机械臂开发强化学习模仿学习PythonC/C++工业机器人运动控制算法机器人算法PyTorch
工作职责 
1. 负责机器人及机械臂端侧软件系统的全流程开发、调试与迭代维护,保障实机运行的稳定性与作业执行效率。
2. 落地机械臂运动控制、任务调度及智能控制算法的开发与验证工作,持续优化机械臂在抓取、装配、插拔等复杂操作场景下的作业精度与抗干扰能力。 
3. 推进强化学习、模仿学习等前沿算法在机器人实体操作任务中的工程化落地,完成算法从仿真环境到真实机械臂的迁移适配与效果调优。 
4. 联动感知、硬件、算法团队完成机器人感知、控制、决策模块的系统集成与跨设备联调,打通从模型训练到实机执行的完整交付链路。 
5. 快速定位并解决机器人现场运行中出现的软件缺陷、控制偏差及算法适配问题,沉淀技术解决方案与工程化规范,提升团队研发效率。
requirements: 1.语言要求:交流熟练掌握粤语、英语
2. 硕士及以上学历,计算机、自动化、机器人、机械电子、控制工程等相关专业,具备扎实的控制理论与软件工程基础。
3. 熟练掌握Linux开发环境,具备Linux环境下软件模块开发、调试及复杂问题排查能力;精通Python或C++至少一门编程语言,能独立完成功能模块的编码实现与性能优化。
4. 掌握机械臂运动学、动力学与控制相关基础理论,具备机械臂实机开发或调试经验,有力控机械臂实际操作与应用经验者优先。

# 无人机-传感器算法专家 你的价值,本该更高. 为了更好地提升城市即时配送的效率与体验,2017年,美团启动了无人机配送服务的探索,通过科技创新推动履约工具变革,加快建设空地协同的本地即时配送网络。. 在过去的六年里,美团无人机完成了飞行器、自动化机场及智能调度系统的研发工作,实现了研发设计、生产制造、运营运维全链条布局,达成了城市复杂场景物流无人机高频次、高密度、多天时、多天侯运行。. 2023年7月,美团无人机在上海发布了自主研发的第四代无人机,跟此前机型相比,新机型升级了环境适应能力,可在“零下20度至50度”的中雨、中雪、6级风、弱光等环境中稳定飞行,能够适应97%以上国内城市的自然环境要求。. 截至2024年12月,美团无人机已在深圳、北京、上海、广州、南京、迪拜等城市开通53条航线,并累计完成订单超40万单。即时零售配送服务覆盖了办公、社区、景区、市政公园、校园、医疗、图书馆等多种场景。在医疗场景中,美团无人机可围绕医疗血液、检验样本、院前急救物资、特殊药品等医疗物资配送需求建设端到端的全天时急送网络。. 1. 负责相机、LiDAR、IMU、Radar 等多传感器系统的标定算法研发,包括离线标定与在线自标定. 1. 扎实的数学基础,熟悉李群李代数、非线性优化、状态估计. 2. 精通相机模型与标定(内参、外参、畸变校正),熟悉 OpenCV. 3. 熟悉 LiDAR-Camera 联合标定流程,熟练使用 PCL、Open3D 等点云库. 4. 熟悉 IMU 标定与 IMU/Camera/LiDAR 融合算法. 5. 熟练掌握 C++,熟悉 Linux 开发环境,具备良好的工程代码能力. 6. 熟悉算法优化与加速,有 CUDA、多线程、嵌入式部署经验优先. 7. 熟练运用AI辅助工具(如代码生成、数据分析、模型调优等)进行算法开发与优化;. 2. 熟悉 VINS-Fusion、ORB-SLAM、LIO-SAM 等开源框架并有二次开发经验. 团队有丰富的算法/软硬件集成经验,丰富的训练资源和落地场景,无惧挑战,从0到1打造了低空物流配送系统。加入后进一步与经验丰富的算法团队共同探索在城市场景中落地人工智能与机器人技术,让科技服务千家万户!. ### 工作地点. ### 公司信息. 已上市 · 10000人以上 · 互联网生活服务(O2O) 已审核 已审核. 工作职责 
1.负责公司核心项目的模型设计、开发、训练、调优;开发基于物理数据验证的世界动作模型,实现物理条件化动作头,提升模型对物理漂移(摩擦、质量、阻尼变化)的鲁棒性。 
2.基于 Diffusion / Flow-Matching 流匹配架构,完成视频 DiT、动作专家DiT、Q-Former 符号提取模块的改造与迭代;实现推理‐渲染解耦、结构化注意力掩码、多模态条件化等核心机制。 
3.基于RoboTwin、LIBERO 仿真基准,完成模型仿真环境训练、消融实验、指标评测;设计对照实验定位模型失效原因,输出实验报告与技术方案。 
4.对接机器人真机链路,完成模型导出、推理部署优化,降低端侧推理时延,完成仿真到真机(Sim2Real)迁移验证。 
5.跟进国际前沿世界模型、WAM、物理语言相关论文,复现、评估、改造前沿算法,转化为内部可用模块。 
6.和数据团队协同,定义世界模型训练数据集格式、Token 处理规范,配合完成数据集迭代;参与技术方案评审、技术文档撰写。
requirements: 1.计算机、自动化、AI、机器人相关硕士及以上学历;有扎实深度学习理论基础,熟悉 Transformer、Diffusion、Flow‐Matching 流匹配;熟练 PyTorch。
2.有大模型 / 视频生成模型 / 扩散模型 / 具身 VLA/WAM 模型实际开发调优经验;有完整模型训练、消融实验、指标评测项目经历。
3.熟悉多模态模型,了解 VAE、Q‐Former、FSQ 离散量化等技术,有 Tokenizer 开发改造经验优先。
4.熟悉至少一套机器人仿真环境:RoboTwin / LIBERO / SAPIEN / Isaac Sim,有仿真环境下模型训练经验优先。

3.有模型推理加速、模型导出部署经验;熟悉 KV Cache、结构化注意力掩码开发。
4.有arxiv 一作 / 二作论文、开源项目贡献、竞赛 top 成绩。
关于我们:美梦空间(Memo)是一家专注于世界模型(World Models)研发与应用的前沿科技公司,由浙江省北大信息技术高等研究院孵化,依托北京大学视频与视觉技术国家工程研究中心和北京大学信息技术高等研究院的科研力量成立。核心团队在具身智能、视频编解码、空间计算、人工智能领域积累了深厚的研究经验,具备顶尖学术和工程水平。

requirements: 1. 具有机器人的控制、规划、感知算法的研究经验,熟悉深度学习,计算机视觉,多模态算法,机器人决策规划控制领域的前沿研究。 2. 极佳的工程实现能力,熟练掌握C/C++、Java、Python等至少一门语言。 3. 具备较强学习能力,对新事物保有好奇心,并能快速适应新环境;良好的沟通能力和团队协同能力;能与他人合作,共同完成目标;对所在领域有热情,不惧困难与挑战,善于独立思考并反思总结。 4. 加分项: 1)有ACM/NOI/IOI、Kaggle、国内外数学大赛、机器学习、深度学习相关竞赛获奖者优先。 2)在国际知名期刊或会议(NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR,ICRA,IROS,CoRL,RSS,CVPR,ICCV,ECCV等)上发表过高水平论文者优先。 3)有多轴机械臂、足式机器人等机器人平台算法研发及工程经验者优先。

jobs.title: AI智能应用工程师招聘_北京榆构有限公司招聘 - 智联招聘
jobs.description:
一、产业大模型日常运维 
1. 负责企业产业大模型运行监控、性能优化、异常排查、日志分析、权限配置和版本管理,保障模型稳定、高效、安全运行。 
2. 完成数据清洗、数据标注、知识库更新、语料迭代、提示词维护等基础运维工作,持续提升模型效果与响应质量。 
3. 组织第三方交付成果的测试验收、问题整改、上线发布和效果复盘,推动问题闭环和版本持续优化。 
二、模型二次开发与功能迭代 
1. 根据生产、销售、技术、质量、设备、经营管理等需求,对第三方搭建的产业大模型进行二次开发、接口改造和功能扩展。 
2. 参与Prompt工程、工作流编排、RAG知识库构建、模型微调和效果调优,提升模型在行业场景中的准确率和实用性。 
3. 开展AI应用脚本开发、接口调用、页面配置和简单后端开发,提高系统适配性和交付效率。 
三、AI应用落地与业务对接 
1. 推动大模型在生产调度、质量管控、成本核算、设备运维、客户技术服务、经营分析等场景落地应用。 
2. 对接各业务部门,梳理AI需求,输出可落地的AI应用方案、功能原型、实施计划及评价指标。 
3. 协同业务部门梳理流程、标准和知识规则,推动AI能力嵌入现有管理流程和业务系统。 
四、系统集成与接口开发 
1. 负责AI大模型与ERP、MES、WMS、OA、设备物联网平台等系统的接口对接、数据互通和联调测试。 
2. 编写接口文档、部署说明、运维手册和操作指引,形成标准化AI应用交付流程。 
3. 配合完成日志管理、访问控制、备份恢复和运行巡检,提升系统可靠性和可维护性。 
五、AI项目管理与成果沉淀 
1. 跟进AI项目进度,协调第三方厂商、内部IT和业务部门完成需求确认、开发联调、测试验收和正式上线。 
2. 建立应用台账、案例库和数据指标看板,沉淀AI场景、优化经验和复用组件,逐步形成公司内部AI能力体系。 
3. 开展用户培训、推广辅导和使用支持,提升员工使用率、应用覆盖率和实际业务价值。 
六、安全与合规管理 
1. 负责模型数据安全、权限管理、敏感信息脱敏和合规审查,确保AI应用符合公司信息安全要求。 
2. 对不符合业务需求、数据质量或安全规范的模型方案和上线版本提出整改建议或暂缓上线建议。 
3. 完成上级交办的其他与AI应用建设、运维和推广相关工作。
requirements: 1、本科及以上学历,计算机科学与技术、软件工程、人工智能、数据科学与大数据技术、自动化、电子信息工程、数学与应用数学、统计学等相关专业;物联网工程、智能制造、工业工程、通信工程等专业优秀者亦可。
2、2年以上AI应用开发、大模型运维、NLP/机器学习项目相关经验,3年以上优先;具有制造业、工业互联网、装备制造、信息化建设项目经验者优先;具备知识库建设、系统接口集成、流程编排、二次开发或项目交付经验者优先。
3、以下证书作为优先或加分项,非硬性强制要求:
(1). 国家职称/软考类:信息系统项目管理师、系统集成项目管理工程师、软件设计师、网络工程师等。
(2). 人工智能/职业技能类:人工智能工程师、人工智能训练师、人工智能应用工程师、生成式人工智能技术应用类证书等。
(3). 云与平台认证类:阿里云、华为云、腾讯云、百度智能云等AI应用开发、模型训练、云计算或大数据相关认证。
(4). 其他相关证书:TensorFlow/PyTorch开发、MLOps/DevOps、数据分析、信息安全、PMP等相关认证。
(5). 持有助理工程师、工程师或高级工程师职称者优先。

jobs.description: VLA Intern (Vision-Language-Action) 方向一句话: 让机器人在我们的仿真场景里"会做事": 跑通并评测 VLA 模型在操作任务上的表现, 把验证过的策略做成演示。 • 用工形式:实习(按天计酬),表现优秀毕业可转全职 • 地点:杭州,线下坐班,每周 4-5 天 • 薪资:400~600 元/天(约合 9,000~13,000 元/月);特别优秀者面议 • 学历:计算机、人工智能、机器人或相关专业在读;硕士/博士优先,有实战的本科生同样欢迎 • 项目证据:必须随简历附一段能证明模型实际跑通的证据(仓库/实验报告/录屏),无证据不予考虑 软件 • PyTorch、Isaac Lab/Isaac Sim 或 MuJoCo、GR00T/pi0/OpenVLA 之一、Python 工作职责 • 在公司仿真场景中运行 GR00T、pi0、OpenVLA 或同类模型的推理、基础训练与微调 • 搭建与调试推理/训练流程: 加载 checkpoint、配置输入输出、分析模型行为 • 在操作(manipulation)任务上对不同模型做横向评测, 清晰记录实验过程与结论 • 将验证过的策略部署到桌面真机做演示, 参与真机与仿真对照内容录制(提供设备与培训)
requirements: 任职要求 • 实际跑过 GR00T、pi0、OpenVLA 之一(课程或实验室项目均可), 能独立完成模型推理与基础微调, 不要求从零训练大模型; 只会调 API 或纯视觉检测的不匹配 • 熟悉 Python 与 PyTorch, 能熟练使用 Linux 和 GPU 环境 • 英语能阅读英文技术文档并进行口头及书面技术沟通(与美国团队协作,技术面试以英文进行) 加分项 • 强化学习(PPO/SAC)或模仿学习经验; Isaac Lab/Isaac Sim/MuJoCo 仿真经验 • 具身智能方向的论文、开源或竞赛成果; 遥操作/真机数据采集经验 申请材料 • 简历 + 模型实际跑通的证据(仓库、实验报告或录屏任选其一), 发送至公司邮箱, 邮件标题: VLA实习生 + 学校 + 姓名 + 每周可到岗天数 + 最快到岗时间

宇泛注重技术创新,拥有浙江省重点企业研究院,曾入选工信部《2024年人工智能赋能新型工业化典型应用案例》,工信部《2021年人工智能产业创新任务揭榜挂帅》揭榜优胜单位,杭州市《2022年人工智能重大科技创新项目》牵头单位,浙江省《2023年“尖兵”“领雁”研发攻关计划》第一参与单位。截至目前,公司已获得有效知识产权343项,其中软著184项 ,发明专利51项,外观设计专利71项,实用新型专利37项;作为主要起草单位主持参与制定已发布国家标准3项,团体标准9项。相关产品和方案迭代至今已在动态人脸识别领域和数智建造领域占据重要地位,获2022年浙江省科学技术进步奖三等奖、2023年中国自动化学会科技进步二等奖、浙江省首版次软件产品、省级工业新产品、杭州市优质产品等多项荣誉。

jobs.description:
实习证明 C/C++助教线下教育
工作内容 
1. 回复学员在学习过程中遇到的技术问题,协助分析并解决代码、软件环境、硬件接线及设备调试等问题。 
2. 完成部分课程内容的讲解,包括基础知识讲解、代码演示、实验操作和项目指导。 
3. 根据课程安排,提前熟悉课程内容、代码和硬件设备,做好课程讲解前的准备。 
4. 协助学员完成课程实验和项目,针对学员遇到的问题进行耐心指导。 
5. 对课程中经常出现的技术问题进行整理,形成常见问题说明或解决方案。 
6. 协助测试课程代码、教学案例和硬件设备,及时反馈发现的问题。 
7. 根据实际情况,协助整理课程资料、示例代码和操作文档。 
8. 配合完成其他与课程教学、技术答疑相关的工作。 
基础要求 
1. 具备一定的C语言基础,能够看懂和修改基础代码。 
2. 具备一定的Python基础,能够完成简单程序编写和基础报错排查。 
3. 了解数字电路、模拟电路相关基础知识。 
4. 能够看懂基础电路图、模块接线图和引脚说明。 
5. 有焊接、接线、电子元器件安装或硬件调试经验。 
6. 对机器人、嵌入式、人工智能、具身智能等方向感兴趣。 
7. 具备较强的学习能力,愿意主动学习没有接触过的新知识。 
8. 遇到问题能够主动查资料、测试和分析,不依赖他人直接给出答案。 
9. 具备一定的语言表达和讲解能力,能够将基础技术知识清楚地讲解给学员。 
10. 有耐心,能够根据不同学员的基础调整讲解方式。 
能力与态度要求 
1. 做事认真、细心,具备较强的责任感。 
2. 有主动思考和主动解决问题的意识。 
3. 遇到不会的内容时愿意主动学习,而不是直接放弃。 
4. 能够独立分析基础技术问题。 
5. 具备一定的逻辑思维能力和问题排查能力。 
6. 有较好的时间观念,能够按时完成安排的事项。 
7. 情绪稳定,能够耐心面对重复性问题。 
8. 能够长期、稳定地参与相关工作。 
9. 对技术有一定兴趣,愿意持续积累和提升。 
10. 不要求目前掌握全部技术,但需要有较强的学习意愿和执行能力。 
11. 回复问题及时,能够持续跟进问题,避免只回复一次后没有后续。 
12. 具备良好的沟通能力和团队协作意识。 
具备以下经验者优先: 
1. 有ESP32、STM32、Arduino等单片机开发经验。 
2. 有机器人、小车、机械臂等相关项目经验。 
3. 使用过编码电机、电机驱动、传感器或IMU。 
4. 接触过ROS2。 
5. 熟悉Linux或Ubuntu基础操作。 
6. 有PyBullet、Gazebo等机器人仿真软件使用经验。 
7. 参加过电子设计、机器人、智能车等相关竞赛。 
8. 有课程助教、教学、技术支持或社群答疑经验。 
9. 有技术文档编写、教程整理或项目复盘经验。 
10. 有可以展示的代码、项目、作品或比赛经历。

jobs.description:
工作职责 
1.技术路线与架构规划 
定义物流人形 VLA 整体技术架构:视觉感知、多模态理解、自然语言任务指令解析、动作生成、全身运动控制、抓取操作闭环;制定 1-3 年物流场景 VLA 技术演进路线。 
2.VLA 模型研发与场景适配 
主导物流专属 VLA 大模型预训练、微调、RLHF / 模仿学习、强化学习落地;针对料箱、纸箱、包裹、不规则货物、货架、托盘做物体识别、姿态估计、6DoF 抓取、场景语义理解、环境动态避障。 
3.物流数据集与仿真平台建设 
搭建物流人形机器人多模态数据集采集、标注、清洗、迭代闭环;基于 Isaac Sim/MuJoCo 搭建物流仓储仿真环境,推进 Sim2Real 迁移,大幅降低真机调试成本。 
4.真机落地与工程化 
主导 VLA 算法与人形本体、运动控制、整机固件、调度系统、仓储 WMS/AGV 系统联调;解决真实仓储光照变化、货物堆叠遮挡、地面不平整、人员混行等复杂工况鲁棒性问题,保证高频稳定作业。 
5.团队管理与跨部门协同 
组建并管理 VLA / 具身智能算法团队,负责招聘、技术攻关、里程碑交付;对接产品、硬件、结构、电控、产线、物流客户,定义场景需求、算法指标、交付标准。 
6.前沿技术引入与专利壁垒 
跟进世界模型、具身大模型、端到端 VLA、扩散策略等前沿,快速落地到物流作业场景;主导技术专利、软著、顶会论文布局。
requirements: 1.硬性要求:计算机科学、人工智能、机器人学、自动化、控制工程、计算机视觉等相关专业博士学历(海外顶尖高校博士优先)。
2.工作经验:3 年以上 VLA / 具身智能 / 人形机器人算法研发经验(含博士期间课题研究及博士后经历),有物流仓储、分拣、抓取、码垛、工业搬运场景算法落地经验者优先。
3.博士期间深耕 VLA 多模态学习、具身智能、强化学习 / 模仿学习等方向,有相关顶会(NeurIPS/ICML/ICRA/IROS/CVPR)论文发表或核心专利产出;
4.精通视觉 - 语言 - 动作多模态架构,熟悉 OpenVLA/RT-2/GR00T/π?等主流人形 VLA 框架,熟练运用 PyTorch/TensorFlow 进行大模型微调与优化;
5.精通机器人 3D 视觉技术(点云处理、深度估计、6DoF 姿态估计、物体检测分割),熟悉 ROS/ROS2、Isaac Sim/MuJoCo 仿真平台及真机部署全流程;
6.具备扎实的数学建模与算法推导能力,能独立攻克物流场景下 VLA 核心技术难题(如杂乱货物抓取、动态避障、Sim2Real 迁移)。
7.核心素质:强技术领导力与项目管理能力,能带领团队完成场景化落地指标;结果导向,具备跨部门(硬件、产品、客户)高效沟通能力;对人形机器人物流场景商业化有深刻理解与执着追求。
博士期间课题聚焦人形机器人或物流机器人相关方向;
有大规模物流机器人多模态数据集构建经验;
主导过物流场景人形机器人 / VLA 算法从原型到量产落地项目。
职位类别:计算机软、硬件/互联网/IT
有怡科技(Hfun?Tech)是一家专注通用具身智能机器人全栈研发的硬科技企业,前身北京有怡科技 2024 年在北京创立,2025 年落户浙江金华金义新区,为金华首家人形机器人产业化项目,获得地方政府基金投资。
公司由航天一院副首席科学家刘轶博士创立,核心团队来自航天一院、小鹏机器人、北理工、浙大等科研院所与头部企业,拥有十余年足式、人形机器人研发积累,曾参与国家 863 四足液压机器人项目,具备运动控制、整机硬件、3D 视觉、具身 AI 完整自研能力。
公司提出“本质人形、定向通用”产品理念,不片面追求外观拟人,聚焦机器人实际作业能力,采用腿臂复用模块化统一硬件平台,一套机体可切换人形、轮式、四足多种形态,降低多场景定制成本。
核心产品矩阵覆盖:T01 可变形本质人形机器人、GEN?HM01 全尺寸人形机器人、IND?HW03 轮式双臂作业机器人、四足特种机器人,同时提供教育开发套件与定制化机器人技术服务。
业务面向 B 端市场,落地智慧仓储物流、工业巡检、半导体新能源工厂、电力特种救援、文旅展厅导览、科研教育等场景,与京东等产业伙伴开展场景联合落地,致力于打造好用、易用、可规模化部署的通用机器人产品,推动具身智能产业真实落地。

jobs.title: 具身智能算法工程师(实习)_积加科技实习_牛客网
jobs.description: 当前需求只招:具身智能,机械臂操作、仿真(数据采集)这两块的人 职位描述: 你有没有想过,机器人什么时候能真正走进千家万户?不是实验室里的“表演秀”,也不是限定场景的“固定动作”——而是像人一样,在杂乱的厨房中准确抓起一个杯子,在堆满衣物的房间里识别出一件T恤,并把它整齐叠好。这条道路注定是艰难的,但是也注定是可达的。 现阶段我们专注于机器人的通用操作能力 (General-purpose Pick & Place)。它不依赖预设规则,也不局限于单一任务,而是能在真实家庭环境中,自主理解空间、决策判断、规划动作、完成操作。如果你也好奇: 机器人如何理解复杂指令,自主推理、决策、规划执行步骤? 多模态感知(视觉、触觉、力觉)如何融合成统一的动作决策? VLA、VLM 等生成式具身模型是否真的能让机器人“边想边做”? 强化学习、MPC、运动规划等控制策略,如何落地到一台真实机器人上? 那这里就是你的理想实验场。欢迎加入我们,一起推动具身智能在通用操作方向上的落地与进化。 岗位职责: 机器人AI算法 1、研究基于多模态大模型(如 Vision-Language-Action, Diffusion Policy 等)的感知、推理与动作生成方法。 2、构建融合视觉、力觉、触觉反馈的规划与控制算法,提升机器人在开放环境中的操作鲁棒性与精细度。 3、开发面向复杂场景的非端到端Manipulation AI模块,涵盖通用物体抓取、Articulated object操作、工具使用/设备交互、以及移动操作中的whole body control等。 机器人软件系统 1、搭建AI Native机器人系统,以AI模型为核心驱动,集成多源感知、记忆机制、任务推理、行为规划与底层控制等模块,支持模块化、可扩展、可持续演进的系统架构。包括但不限于: 移动底盘与机械臂的协同控制系统。 基于任务语义的跨模态行为决策系统。 整合AI算法、运动规划、操作控制等模块,打造全链路任务执行引擎。 2、利用仿真环境(如Isaac Sim、PyBullet、MuJoCo等)开展算法训练、系统集成测试与虚拟验证。
requirements: 职位要求: 1、学历背景:计算机、人工智能、机械工程、电子工程、自动化、机器人学等相关专业硕士及以上学历。 2、算法基础:具备以下至少一个领域的扎实基础:深度学习、大模型、计算机视觉;视觉-触觉融合;SLAM;Manipulation AI;机器人学、路径规划、运动控制等。 3、编程技能:至少精通一门语言,如C++、Python;具备良好的软件工程能力;算法研发需掌握常见的深度学习框架;软件研发需熟悉常见的机器人开发框架、仿真环境。 4、项目经验:有丰富的模型训练、调优和部署经验;有机器人项目研发经验。 5、团队合作:具备良好的沟通能力和团队合作精神,能够高效推动技术方案落地。 6、创新精神:对机器人技术充满热情,具备主动探索能力与持续学习的动力。 7、优先条件:有顶会论文发表、机器人领域竞赛获奖、相关技术专利或开源项目贡献经验者优先;有知名机器人或自动驾驶公司的工作经验优先。

PyTorchTensorFlowPythonC++算法研究机器学习人工智能
1、参与具身智能大模型前沿算法研究,包括框架设计、模型优化、面向操作/导航等下游任务的微调与部署;探索结合视觉-动作映射的“感知→决策→执行”端到端闭环。 
2、参与可穿戴设备(数据手套、遥操作/动捕系统)的数据采集与处理,完成从本体采集数据到训练样本的转换、动作重定向与数据治理。 
3、参与机器本体上的算法验证与真机系统集成:面向机械臂、双臂协调及足式机器人,实现路径规划、轨迹优化、力控/阻抗控制等规控算法的设计、仿真与实机部署调试。 
4、基于仿真平台(Isaac Sim、MuJoCo等)构建训练环境,完成Sim-to-Real算法评测,并在真机上做行为验证与在环测试,提升操作鲁棒性与成功率。 
5、参与 Linux/ROS2 环境下的传感器驱动调试、嵌入式控制与运动控制 SDK 开发,保障本体系统稳定运行。 
1、计算机、人工智能、自动化、控制、机器人、机械等相关专业在校本科/硕士及以上,有相关方向研究或项目经历者优先。 
2、扎实的数学与编程基础,熟悉深度学习理论;精通Python,熟悉 PyTorch/TensorFlow(模型研发方向)。 
3、掌握机器人运动学/动力学基础,了解 MPC、轨迹优化、模仿学习(ACT、Diffusion Policy)或强化学习运动控制方案(规控方向)。 
4、熟悉 C++、Linux 与 ROS/ROS2,了解多线程、实时性与常用通信协议;有传感器驱动或嵌入式开发经验(嵌入式方向)。 
5、了解遥操作、动作捕捉、可穿戴数据采集流程,或有真机调试经验者优先。

| 我们正在建设面向具身智能的仿真训练与真实场景执行系统。该岗位的最终目标不是只在仿真中获得较高成功率,而是让机器人进入真实的商店、客厅、厨房等场景,安全、稳定地完成导航、抓取、放置、整理和人与机器人协作等任务。该岗位负责打通从仿真场景、任务与数据构建,到策略训练、真机集成、现场调试和真实任务评测的完整链路。候选人需要具备良好的机器人系统与 Python 工程能力,能够定位感知、规划、控制、通信、硬件和环境之间的系统性问题,并对机器人在真实场景中的最终执行结果负责。## 工作职责- 在 RoboCasa、MuJoCo、Isaac Sim、SAPIEN、ManiSkill、robosuite 或其他平台中搭建机器人仿真场景。- 将 3D 资产转换并配置为 USD、URDF、MJCF 等仿真格式,完成尺度、坐标系、碰撞体、质量、摩擦力、关节和物理属性设置。- 根据真实商店、客厅、厨房等目标环境构建数字化场景,配置机器人、相机、光照、传感器和可操作物体,并控制仿真与实景之间的关键差异。- 设计具身智能任务,明确 instruction、initial state、action space、success condition、failure condition、reset distribution 和 benchmark split。- 为模仿学习、强化学习、Diffusion Policy、ACT、VLA 和 LeRobot 等训练流程生成、清洗和管理轨迹数据。- 将仿真或数据训练得到的策略部署到真实机器人,完成模型转换、推理服务、机器人接口、传感器接入和控制链路集成。- 在真实场景中完成机器人标定、定位、导航、抓取与操作调试,包括相机内外参、手眼标定、坐标系、末端执行器和动作精度校准。- 设计并实施 sim-to-real 方案,包括域随机化、系统辨识、真实数据回采、策略微调和仿真参数校准。- 组织真实机器人任务测试,建立现场部署、任务初始化、失败恢复、人工接管、日志回传和重复实验流程。- 分析真机失败案例,区分感知、规划、控制、通信、策略、硬件和场景因素,并推动问题闭环。- 为真实环境中的人员、设备和物体制定安全约束,落实速度与力限制、碰撞保护、急停、工作空间限制和异常降级机制。- 开发自动化场景与任务检查工具,检测穿模、碰撞体错误、动力学异常、不可达、不可抓取、任务无法重置和成功判定失效等问题。- 建立贯通仿真与真机的可复现训练和评测 pipeline,对比成功率、碰撞率、恢复率、任务耗时、泛化能力和 sim-to-real gap。- 设计场景、物体、初始状态和语言指令的随机化方案,并控制训练集、验证集和测试集之间的泛化难度。- 使用 Codex 等 Agent 工具辅助代码开发、批量实验、数据清洗、结果分析和失败案例归因。- 与生成式 AI Agent 与 3D 资产工程师协作定义资产接入标准,与世界模型研究工程师协作定义交互数据和策略接口。- 参与机器人学习、sim-to-real、真实场景部署和 benchmark 方向的创新研究与论文工作。##
requirements: - 熟悉 Python,能够独立完成仿真环境、数据处理、实验脚本和自动化工具开发。- 理解机器人学基础,包括坐标变换、位姿、运动学、轨迹、碰撞检测、传感器和控制等概念。- 具有真实机器人开发或实验经验,能够进行设备连接、标定、动作调试、日志分析和故障排查。- 熟悉 Linux 环境,能够使用 ROS 或 ROS 2 完成机器人、传感器和算法模块之间的集成。- 了解机器人操作、导航、模仿学习或强化学习中的至少一个方向,并理解从模型输出到真实机器人动作执行的完整链路。- 理解 mesh、碰撞体、质量、摩擦力、关节、材质、相机和尺度等仿真资产概念。- 能够定义清晰、可执行、可自动评测的机器人任务,并将同一任务协议落实到仿真和真实环境。- 具备较强的问题拆解、现场调试和工程执行能力,愿意参与真实场景搭建、真机实验和迭代部署。## 加分项- 熟悉 MuJoCo、RoboCasa、robosuite、Isaac Sim、SAPIEN、ManiSkill 或 Habitat 中的一个或多个平台。- 熟悉 imitation learning、reinforcement learning、Diffus

articles.title: Phoenix: Learning Scene Structure Representations for Generalizable World-Action Models
articles.summary: World-action models jointly predict future observations and actions, yet reconstruction-oriented visual representations do not explicitly emphasize the spatial relationships and object-state changes needed for manipulation. We introduce Phoenix, which learns representations of scene structure for world-action modeling. Specifically, Phoenix Encoder enriches DINOv3's general visual semantics through dual-teacher distillation of geometric and spatiotemporal semantic knowledge. Next, CS-VAE causally aggregates and compresses Phoenix Encoder features into generative latents while preserving scene information and spatial layout. Finally, Phoenix jointly predicts these latents, complementary appearance latents, and robot actions, linking scene evolution with action generation. articles.summary: Learning shared action representations is central to cross-embodiment manipulation. articles.summary: Egocentric human recordings are far cheaper than dexterous robot demonstrations, promising stronger pretraining and direct skill learning without task-specific robot data. This raises two questions: how human data should supervise the policy, and how a dexterous robot should read out actions at deployment. articles.summary: Tendon-driven robots, which actuate like biological muscles by using motors to wind wires, offer advantages such as variable stiffness and redundant actuation. Despite these advantages, musculoskeletal structures inherently involve a large number of diverse muscles, making it desirable to compactly modularize each muscle unit and flexibly accommodate diverse muscle arrangements. While various small muscle modules have been proposed to date, existing designs tend to be complex, difficult to maintain, and suffer from low backdrivability and limited actuation speed due to their high gear ratios. In this work, we propose QDD-MM, a muscle module that leverages recent advances in quasi-direct-drive motors to achieve a simpler and more compact structure with higher backdrivability and faster actuation than previous modules. articles.title: Old Experience, New Lessons: Relabeling Autonomous Robot Rollouts in Interactive Imitation Learning
articles.summary: Interactive imitation learning enables robots to learn from human interventions during deployment. These interactions naturally produce sparse human corrections and abundant autonomous robot experience without human action labels. Yet existing methods either leave this experience unused for action supervision or imitate historical robot actions, which can reinforce suboptimal behavior. To address this limitation, we propose Set-valued Relabeling of Autonomous experience (SeRA), a framework that learns from autonomous robot experience through set-valued supervision of policy relabels. Later policy checkpoints relabel this experience, and agreement across checkpoints filters the relabels. Since agreement does not guarantee correctness, SeRA constructs desired action sets around accepted relabels. articles.title: ProbeShare: Probing a Few, Sharing Across Many for Fast World-Model Planning
articles.summary: Visual planning with a frozen joint-embedding world model supports robotic reaching and object manipulation by evaluating candidate action sequences against an image goal before execution. Standard cross-entropy method (CEM) planners roll out every candidate independently through a billion-parameter predictor, even when nearby actions induce similar scene changes. This redundant computation grows with population size and search rounds, slowing closed-loop replanning. We observe that candidates within a planning step share an observation history and thus a common action-to-feature map. Based on this insight, we propose ProbeShare, which measures local responses with a few representative probes and reconstructs each candidate's feature grid through scene-conditioned, geometry-aware weighting. articles.title: TapTacTouch: Shape Completion from Sparse Tactile Contacts with Geometric Priors
articles.summary: 3D object reconstruction is essential for robotic perception and manipulation, yet conventional approaches predominantly rely on visual observations that can be limited by occlusion or unavailable in visually constrained environments. In this work, we propose a vision-free, training-free, and category-agnostic framework for reconstructing 3D object meshes from sparse tactile contacts without relying on pretrained shape models. A 6-DoF robotic arm equipped with a 20-DoF multi-finger robotic hand collects tactile observations using 3x3 pressure sensor arrays mounted on the finger pads. The acquired tactile measurements are transformed into 3D contact constraints through robot kinematics and integrated into a multi-scale Gaussian Process Implicit Surface (GPIS). articles.title: Ego2X: Contact-aware Transfer from Egocentric Human Data to Any Robot
articles.summary: Embodied models depend on real interaction data, yet collecting it on physical robots is slow and labor-intensive. Recent ego-to-robot pipelines retarget first-person view human videos to robot data via transferring hand and arm motion. They judge fidelity mainly by visual appearance. However, trajectories often fail in terms of physics: fingers hover beside objects, and grippers close on empty space. We argue that how the object moves and the contacts that drive the motion count. Thus, we present Ego2X, an object-centric framework that converts monocular egocentric video into physically executable robot data across dexterous hands and parallel grippers. Ego2X centers on CORE (Contact-centric Object-interaction REpresentation), which records each contact on the object by its surface anchor, as well as relative force, grasp mode, and interaction state. articles.title: Lost Between Mind, Model Collaboration, and Motion: Understanding and Measuring Cross-Model Action Misalignment in Commercial Robots
articles.summary: Embodied robots increasingly rely on large language models (LLMs) to interpret user intent and coordinate with robot-specific action models for physical interaction. This multi-model pipeline creates a critical semantic boundary across mind, model collaboration, and motion: semantic consistency may break between what the large model understands, how the small action model translates that understanding into executable commands, and what physical actions the robot ultimately performs. As a security consequence, commercial robots may execute unintended physical actions even when user inputs contain no explicit action commands. To measure this problem, we develop TARS, a black-box framework that explores the command-reasoning-action pipeline and automatically discovers and validates unintended physical behaviors. articles.title: SemPhys: Semantic-Physical Co-Learning for Humanoid Motion Generation via Differentiable World Models
articles.summary: In human-robot collaboration, natural language lets people direct a humanoid's whole-body movements without programming joint trajectories. A common approach generates a kinematic reference from an instruction and relies on a tracking controller to execute it. However, as the controller maintains balance under contact constraints, the executed motion can depart from the reference in ways that change the action it conveys. Our central insight is that semantic alignment must be evaluated directly on the complete motion the robot physically executes. Building on this insight, we introduce \textbf{SemPhys}, a framework that trains motion generators using semantic feedback from simulated executions. A differentiable world model and a fixed tracking controller predict a short segment of a recorded execution. articles.title: WAM-Policy: World Action Models with On-Policy Distillation for Quadrupedal Loco-Manipulation
articles.summary: Arm-free quadrupeds can perform loco-manipulation, walking on three legs while manipulating with a front leg, yet no existing policy for it follows language instructions. World action models (WAMs) have emerged as effective language-conditioned manipulation policies, but are pretrained for robot arms and sample slowly. WAM-Policy turns one WAM into a quadrupedal loco-manipulation policy via two stages. The first, Cross-Morphology Policy Adaptation and Acceleration, adapts the arm-centric WAM to quadrupeds and distills the transferred policy into a student with one video and two action steps by on-policy self-distillation (OPSD). This student, however, is bounded by its teacher, which only imitates demonstrations. The second stage, Task-Specific Improvement and Merging, therefore tunes the teacher by reinforcement learning (RL) and merges the slow specialists into one few-step student by multi-teacher on-policy distillation (M-OPD). articles.title: LaST1.0: A Unified Latent World-Action Model with Control-Centric SpatioTemporal Reasoning
articles.summary: World-Action Models couple action learning with future prediction, enabling robotic policies to capture environmental dynamics for robust control. However, prevailing methods take a reconstruction-oriented approach to model future videos, allocating substantial capacity to appearance details that are incidental to control. In this work, we reformulate world modeling for manipulation as control-centric future prediction in latent space, and present LaST1.0, a unified latent World-Action Model. Rather than modeling an observation-complete video future, LaST1.0 predicts compact, geometry-aware latent targets derived from future wrist views, focusing the supervision on the evolving robot-object interactions required for fine-grained manipulation. To better support this control-centric paradigm, LaST1.0 revisits the visual input interface and attention mechanism of its unified architecture. articles.title: CoRA-VTLA: Contact-Guided Attention and Queryable Response Memory for Tactile Post-Training
articles.summary: In precision manipulation, small errors in alignment or force can cause jamming or deformation, making contact feedback essential for adapting pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) models to these tasks. A single tactile observation leaves the response to recent actions ambiguous. Direct tactile fusion during post-training can also disperse the action expert's visual attention and reduce the share it allocates to contact regions. To address these challenges, CoRA-VTLA augments pretrained VLAs with lightweight tactile modules. A queryable action-response memory retrieves recent contact responses so that the action expert can combine them with immediate tactile feedback. Contact-guided gaze supervision concentrates the visual attention of the tactile semantic token on image regions corresponding to fingertip contact. articles.title: 3DTouch: A Tactile-aware VLA Model with 3D Geometric Relations for Dexterous Manipulation
articles.summary: In contact-rich dexterous manipulation, occlusion by the fingers and interacting objects obscures local geometry, preventing visual observations from fully capturing contact locations. Visually similar scenes may also differ subtly in the relative positions of interacting objects, leading to different contact states. We propose 3DTouch, a tactile-geometric conditioning approach for vision-language-action (VLA) models. 3DTouch constructs a shared 3D visuo-tactile representation by expressing RGB-D scene points and dense five-finger tactile measurements in the robot-base frame, preserving each taxel's spatial location and force vector. Hand-object and object-object relations derived from hand landmarks and pose-aligned reconstructed surfaces explicitly describe the relative arrangement of interacting entities. articles.title: GTI: Grounding Task Intent Throughout Long-Horizon VLA Manipulation
articles.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models generate local actions from visual observations, language, and robot state, but long-horizon manipulation requires the global task intent to remain grounded in the currently executable context. We propose GTI (Grounding Task Intent), which uses the current observation and execution history to localize the active subtask and its execution phase. For the same local subtask, GTI generates two phase-dependent visual targets: an interaction/contact state and a local completion state. The local language instruction and the corresponding phase-specific visual target jointly condition the VLA, specifying both what to do now and what state should be reached at the current phase. During execution, anomaly monitoring and local recovery re-establish an intent-consistent execution context through rollback, re-observation, and phase re-evaluation after persistent deviation. articles.title: ReLoco: Unified Humanoid Locomotion and Fall Recovery via Behavior-Conditioned Motion Priors
articles.summary: Humanoid robots must recover from falls and resume commanded motion to sustain locomotion. Learning these behaviors in one policy requires supervision that accommodates both upright movement and ground-contact recovery. We present ReLoco, a framework that uses behavior-conditioned adversarial motion priors to learn locomotion, get-up from arbitrary fallen postures, and command resumption within one proprioceptive policy. During training, robot posture selects the expert pool and conditions a shared discriminator with two behavior-specific outputs. Task rewards and shared regularization support command tracking and recovery, while temporary assistance facilitates exploration. A simulation-based refinement stage supplies robot-executed motion references for this supervision. articles.title: LAGR: Language-Aware Grasp Re-Ranking for Task Oriented Grasping
articles.summary: Grasping is a fundamental capability for robotic manipulation, with the appropriate grasp depending on the downstream task. For example, a hammer should be held by its handle for hammering but by its head when it is handed over. Selecting such a grasp requires consideration of two criteria: physical feasibility on the object and suitability for the task. Developing such an approach requires dense grasp labels with both feasibility and task scores on real observations, but existing task-oriented grasping datasets are small, synthetic, or costly to annotate. To address this gap, we construct a dataset of 2.68 million scored 5-DoF grasp annotations over 100,911 image-task pairs from $17$ object categories. Additionally, we introduce LAGR, a task-oriented grasp detection method that explicitly addresses both these challenges. articles.title: RePlan-VLA: Progress-Aware Replanning for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Models
articles.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising paradigm for general-purpose robotic manipulation, yet their performance often degrades on long-horizon tasks that require multiple interdependent manipulations. Instead of burdening the VLA policies with long-horizon reasoning, memory, action generation, progress tracking, and error recovery, we argue for leveraging their short-horizon manipulation capabilities within an execution-aware framework. To this end, we introduce \textnormal{\textbf{RePlan-VLA}}, a VLA-agnostic framework that translates a VLA's short-horizon capabilities into reliable long-horizon execution. RePlan-VLA explicitly monitors the robot's motion for progress evaluation, and adaptively revises the future plan based on observed outcomes. We preserve the underlying VLA policy entirely, requiring no additional fine-tuning. articles.title: TacPilot: Does Touch Need to Be Everywhere?
articles.summary: Tactile feedback helps visual manipulation policies respond to local contact, but changes in tactile observations do not always require corrective motion, and sustained corrections do not always require new tactile features. We introduce TacPilot, a tactile residual framework that separates representation updates from action intervention around a frozen visual policy. TacPilot uses a perception gate to determine when tactile features need refreshing and updates only affected regions while reusing unchanged features. A separate intervention gate determines whether bounded Cartesian and gripper residuals modify the nominal visual action. This separation allows tactile perception and action correction to follow different spatial and temporal demands during manipulation. articles.title: CoT-WAM: Collaborative Training of Vision-Language Models and World-Action Models via Plan Latents
articles.summary: General robot manipulation requires both semantic competence and physical foresight. World action models (WAMs) acquire an understanding of and predictive capability over the physical world by jointly modeling visual foresight and action distributions. However, existing WAMs still lack semantic competence: they have limited ability to perform open-world scene understanding, semantic reasoning, and long-horizon planning. Although vision-language models (VLMs) provide these capabilities, effectively integrating their semantic priors into WAM prediction and control remains challenging. To address this challenge, we propose CoT-WAM, a jointly trained WAM-VLM framework. CoT-WAM uses a learnable embedding to exchange information between the VLM and the WAM, which is supervised by textual and goal-image signals during training to encode rich intent information. articles.title: Improve How You Improve: Recursive Policy Self-Improvement for Zero-Shot Open-Vocabulary Multi-Object Navigation
articles.summary: To advance the development of embodied general navigation, zero-shot open-vocabulary multi-object navigation has attracted increasing attention, aiming to enable robots to efficiently search multiple objects in unseen environments without training. For this task, the key lies in improving navigation policies from earlier searches to locate subsequent goals more efficiently. Recent methods automate this process through trajectory reflection and rule revision, enabling policy self-improvement. However, the mechanisms for diagnosing problems and generating revisions are typically designed by humans and remain fixed across iterations. Consequently, the system's capacity for continued self-improvement remains constrained, even as its navigation policy evolves. articles.title: ZERITH V2.5: From Predictive Power to Policy Learnability
articles.summary:
When humans learn to manipulate an unfamiliar object, they may already be able to anticipate how its state will change while still being unable to control it skillfully. This gap between prediction and control motivates us to study how the priors acquired by video generation models can be used effectively by an action policy. We present ZERITH V2.5, a video-action model (VAM) in which the action policy reads intermediate features of a video generation model, and use it to study, under fixed demonstrations and a fixed total number of updates, what kind of predictive training improves subsequent action learning.
 We find that the way video predictive training is supervised affects subsequent action learning. articles.title: RecallFlow: Episodic Memory as the Source Distribution of Generative Robot Policies
articles.summary: Diffusion and flow-matching policies have become a standard choice for visuomotor imitation learning, owing to their ability to model multimodal action distributions. In memory-dependent manipulation, the robot must act on information that is no longer visible. Existing methods feed the observation history to the policy as an additional condition, while action generation still starts from Gaussian noise. However, the policy must then pick out the relevant target from a long and redundant history, leading to spurious correlations and unreliable decisions as the memory load grows. Additionally, the initial noise carries no information about what the robot has seen, leaving generation without guidance toward the remembered target. articles.title: ExecGap: Exploiting Command-Execution Gap for Patch Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models
articles.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have become a powerful paradigm for robotic manipulation and show strong promise for real-world deployment, making adversarial robustness critical for reliable robot operation. Existing adversarial attacks on VLA-controlled robots mainly optimize prediction-level discrepancies or rollout-level deviations to disrupt manipulation. However, they rarely account for the fact that VLA-predicted commands are not executed directly, but must be realized through downstream control and robot embodiment. In this paper, we propose ExecGap, an adversarial patch attack framework that exploits this command-execution gap to expose embodiment-specific execution vulnerabilities. articles.title: TCP4D: A Unified Tool-Center-Point Tracking and Generation Model for Robot Manipulation
articles.summary: Robot manipulation videos provide a rich visual experience, yet recovering robot action and gripper-state annotations from RGB observations still remains challenging. Using the embodiment-agnostic tool-center-point (TCP) pose as the action space, we present TCP4D, a unified model in which a shared 4D scene representation both tracks observed TCP motion and generates future TCP trajectories. Given a monocular video and initial 2D TCP queries, the tracker directly recovers metric TCP poses in SE(3) and gripper states alongside scene geometry and camera parameters. The generator samples local features from the same 4D representation along the recovered TCP tracks, then combines them with robot observations and language instructions to predict future TCP states. articles.title: PAIR: Bringing Household Robots into the Smart Home
articles.summary: Household robots often need to operate appliances, and smart appliances offer both control panels and device APIs. Existing embodied AI simulation environments, however, model appliances solely as physical objects. We introduce PAIR, a smart-home simulation environment grounded in the Matter protocol~\footnote{https://csa-iot.org/all-solutions/matter/}, the industry standard for smart-home devices. PAIR provides 84 smart-device assets whose functional control panels and APIs act on a shared device state, with ambient conditions that evolve in response to both. From a survey of 1,443 requests, we construct a benchmark of 40 tasks that all require object manipulation yet remain solvable without API access, with 340 human demonstrations for policy training. articles.title: RFW-S: Everyday Deformable Objects with Independent Simulation Verification
articles.summary: Large-scale robotic simulation requires diverse deformable objects with executable physical properties and realistic interaction behaviors. However, existing 3D asset collections primarily emphasize visual diversity, while scalable physical construction and verification remain challenging. We introduce RFW-S, a large-scale dataset of 83,365 simulation-verified assets spanning 485 everyday categories across five structural families: soft solids, cloth sheets, shells, garments, and bags. We develop an automated pipeline integrating reference-guided 3D generation, structure-aware physical modeling, and LLM-assisted parameter estimation and calibration. articles.title: Physics-Informed Tactile-based Shape Estimation of Deformable Linear Objects
articles.summary: Accurate shape estimation of Deformable Linear Objects (DLOs) is a fundamental challenge in robotic manipulation, often hindered by visual occlusions and the high-dimensional configuration space of flexible materials. While Force/Torque (F/T) and vision-centric methods have been proposed, they frequently struggle with grasp-site ambiguities and environmental interference. In this letter, we investigate the hypothesis that global shape estimation can be achieved through tactile sensing and proprioception, without any visual perception. We contend that dense, high-resolution tactile imprints capture critical boundary conditions and contact gradients that are sufficient to resolve the high-dimensional configuration of the DLO. articles.title: Fly as Instructed: Refining World-Action Policies for UAV Vision-Language Navigation
articles.summary: Natural language-guided UAV navigation enables intuitive human-robot interaction and flexible autonomous flight in complex environments. However, reliable navigation requires accurate instruction following, continuous task progress tracking, and safe obstacle avoidance, which remain challenging for existing world-action models that primarily focus on action prediction. articles.title: Technical Report of Mobile Manipulator Robot for Industrial Environments
articles.summary: This paper presents the design and implementation of Auriga Robotics' mobile manipulator robot, developed at the Robotics and Intelligent Automation Laboratory, Department of Electrical Engineering, Shahid Beheshti University. Hereafter, this platform is referred to as the @Work Robot. The robot targets industrial tasks, with an emphasis on improving efficiency in repetitive or hazardous work environments. It uses a 4-wheel Mecanum drive for omnidirectional movement and a 5-degree-of-freedom manipulator arm with a 3D-printed gripper for object handling and navigation. articles.title: Zero-Shot Compositional Generalization for Embodied Manipulation
articles.summary: Robot demonstrations are collected on different embodiments, leaving many robot-skill combinations unobserved. Pooling these data shares visual knowledge, while joint labels remain tied to the demonstrating kinematic chain. We propose a geometry-supervised training framework for zero-shot composition of familiar robots and skills. The central insight is that a demonstrated command provides a tool-space target for every robot that can realize it. Native reconstruction retains demonstrated configurations, and positive reachability checks select targets for cross-robot supervision. articles.title: Network-Exposed Configuration Attacks on LLM-Controlled Social Robots
articles.summary: Large language models (LLMs) in embodied robots create security dependencies beyond inference. We investigate a network-exposed configuration attack on the Pollen Robotics Reachy Mini Lite, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to replace personality settings and the cloud LLM's system prompt through a management interface, without adversarial conversational input. articles.title: Body Schema Policy: Body as the Vision-Action Interface for Efficient Robot Loco-Manipulation
articles.summary: Currently, robots can learn whole-body loco-manipulation through scale: the strongest policies have billions of parameters and still need task-specific fine-tuning. Humans have limited processing capacity, yet learn and act efficiently through a body schema that organizes what they see and how they move. We introduce Body Schema Policy (BSP), an imitation learning policy that builds such a schema into the vision-action interface. Its latent body schema places joint and link tokens on the robot's kinematic tree, where learned screw motions carry features between links. Through body-queried vision, each body part retrieves its own visual evidence, which conditions the denoising of its actions. With this inductive bias, BSP returns an action chunk faster than any policy we compare. articles.title: Learning Accurate End-Effector Trajectory Tracking with Inertial Feedback for a Quadruped Manipulator
articles.summary: Accurate end-effector trajectory tracking on quadruped manipulators is challenging because uncertainties in actuators, foot-ground contact, and geometric errors are propagated through the leg-arm kinematic chain. Detecting such errors requires sensing beyond joint encoders that can capture the effects of these uncertainties on the robot's motion, since joint encoders only provide measurements at the actuated joints and cannot fully observe mechanical errors such as backlash, dimensional inaccuracies, or structural deformation. This work addresses these challenges using a reinforcement learning framework with end-effector (EE) inertial feedback, targeting local high-accuracy manipulation while maintaining a nominal body pose and support configuration without intentional body motion or foot repositioning. articles.title: VSpark: Speculative Decoding for Autoregressive Vision-Language-Action Models
articles.summary: Our aim is to accelerate autoregressive vision-language-action models (VLAs), which generate robot actions one token at a time. articles.summary: Generalised referring expression comprehension (GREC) aims to identify and localise the zero, one or multiple objects referred to by a language expression. However, grounding expert models are sensitive to instruction variation, while generative vision--language models (VLMs) struggle with complete target recovery and rejection of absent targets. articles.title: Task Convergent Flow Matching for Generative Robotics
articles.summary: Successful manipulation requires the manipulated objects to progress toward a desired task outcome. Generative policies can produce plausible robot motions without ensuring this progress, allowing successive action chunks to stall or undo earlier changes to the scene. We introduce a task-centric inference-time refinement framework for flow matching policies that evaluates candidate action chunks through parallel physics-based rollouts and searches for motions satisfying sufficient conditions for task convergence. articles.title: Distilling World Action Models for Efficient Bimanual Manipulation via Anchored Path Matching
articles.summary: World Action Models (WAMs) jointly generate future video and robot actions through iterative denoising. Few-step distillation reduces the number of model evaluations, but its coarse updates can move the student away from the teacher's trajectory. articles.summary: Existing agentic manipulation systems treat pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) policies as opaque, language-only primitives: when a policy call fails under unfamiliar instructions or scene perturbations, the agent cannot steer its behavior and is forced into futile retries or costly manual takeover. We present InteractVLA, a framework that turns pretrained flow-based VLAs into geometrically steerable and inspectable tools through a bidirectional geometric interface with vision-language agents. articles.summary: Visual world models predict future visual states conditioned on actions, but recursive errors in entity poses and spatial relations limit their long-horizon prediction for robot planning and control. We ask whether a separately predicted relational state can correct this drift without restructuring the visual model. This is challenging because graph nodes and visual states share neither elements nor a feature space. We propose Joint Graph--Visual Dynamics Correction (JointGV), a plug-in based on a cross-granularity dynamics hypothesis: despite their different representations, graph-node and visual-state changes describe the same physical transition. JointGV rolls out a task-conditioned scene graph alongside the visual world model, couples their predicted changes, and combines the resulting graph-motion context with graph-predicted node positions to compute a bounded residual. articles.title: Progress Predicts Policy
articles.summary: A task specifies how the world should change, while a policy specifies what the robot should do. We introduce Progress Predicts Policy (PPP), which learns a language-conditioned scalar field through the commands induced by its differential. We obtain action conditioning by composing a latent progress field with a shared world model and read its action gradient at a fixed reference command. Continuous commands scale this gradient by a learned positive gain, while discrete commands use finite differences of the same scalar. This yields a hybrid policy without a separate action head or iterative search. Fitting demonstration progress values alone does not ensure that action gradients align with expert commands. PPP trains the induced commands by imitation and uses double backpropagation for the continuous gradient readout to shape the field's local control geometry. articles.title: Manufacturing Differential Sparsity: Planner-Hardware Co-Design for Efficient World Model Planning
articles.summary: JEPA-style latent world models let embodied agents plan toward new goals with model predictive control, but they are still too slow for real-life embodied control: sampling-based MPC repeats predictor inference tens of thousands of times per plan, and even on high-end GPUs one planning step can take tens of seconds. We observe substantial latent locality in this repeated-inference workload: the predictor maps close actions to close latents, and inside a quantized predictor this closeness takes a form that hardware can exploit, differential bit-level sparsity. Unlike an input stream, whose temporal similarity is given, a planner itself decides which candidates it evaluates together, so the planner can choose its own references and, with reference forest sampling, manufacture more sparsity: it couples the sampled action sequences of each group to a shared root, with competitive planning quality. articles.title: Autonomous Track Racing with a Commercially Available Humanoid: System Design and Real-World Deployment
articles.summary: Learning-based methods now let humanoids run robustly, and they have begun to compete in athletic events. Yet few reports describe a complete autonomous humanoid running system in an actual race, where the robot must follow a lane at a new venue, pace itself within hardware limits, and finish without intervention. We report such a system deployed on the Unitree G1, a commercially available general-purpose humanoid, in the 100 m, 400 m, and 1500 m events of the World Humanoid Robot Games 2026. The system integrates vision-based lane perception, path tracking, and a running policy trained by reinforcement learning with a human motion prior. To address the challenges of humanoid running, we stabilize head-camera images against body motion and use IMU-assisted leg odometry to bridge flight phases. articles.title: ROSMonitoring in Action: Runtime Monitoring and Enforcement for ROS 2 Actions
articles.summary: Robotic applications often rely on long-running operations, such as navigation, manipulation, and inspection, which in ROS~2 are commonly implemented as actions. Unlike topics and services, actions involve a structured lifecycle comprising goal submission and acceptance, feedback, status updates, result retrieval, and cancellation. Existing versions of ROSMonitoring support topics and services, but do not reconstruct this lifecycle or expose action-level events to a runtime-verification oracle. In this paper, we extend ROSMonitoring with runtime monitoring and enforcement for ROS~2 actions. Actions are declared directly in the monitoring configuration and automatically instrumented through the underlying ROS~2 communication endpoints. The generated monitor reconstructs action-level events, correlates them through goal identifiers, maintains the state of active goals, and translates violations into protocol-aware enforcement operations. articles.title: CoBoVLA: Decoupling Language from Action with Discrete Codes for Robust and Interpretable Robot Manipulation
articles.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models achieve high success rates on the LIBERO benchmark but remain sensitive to paraphrasing. Existing VLAs ranging from 0.6B to 7.5B parameters experience a 22-52 point performance drop on LIBERO-Para while SmolVLA exhibits an even larger decline, from 83\% to 8\%. Because most VLAs jointly learn language understanding and action generation, it is difficult to determine whether a failure originates from misunderstanding an instruction or executing it incorrectly. To address these challenges, we introduce CoBoVLA, or CodeBookVLA, a 250M-parameter VLA that decouples language understanding, planning, and control through learned discrete interpretable codes. A text encoder maps the instructions to shared step codes, which a visual planner then converts into action code sequences executed by a language-independent actor. articles.title: Hidden Variables Behind Real-Robot Data Quality: Lessons from Hundreds of Thousands of Hours
articles.summary: As real-robot data collection scales, collection-system design shapes both operator efficiency and the behaviors learned by robot policies. Workspace limitations, control-interface friction, and latency can introduce pauses, detours, and corrective motions into otherwise successful demonstrations. We investigate these effects across embodiment, teleoperation control, and data consistency, combining a kinematic study of 25 dual-arm robots, controlled teleoperation experiments, and real-robot evaluation of fine-tuned $π_{0.5}$ policies. The embodiment study shows that positional reachability overstates orientation-aware task coverage and that modest shoulder motion can substantially expand the effective workspace. Teleoperation experiments show that parallelizing body-part control reduces task completion time by 43-53%, while compliant control improves success and reduces peak contact forces on constrained and contact-rich tasks. articles.title: Beyond Episodic Recall: Experience-to-Knowledge Evolution for Lifelong Embodied Navigation
articles.summary: Lifelong embodied navigation requires agents to accumulate experience through continuous interaction and reuse it for subsequent goal searches. Existing memory-enhanced methods typically retain historical observations or construct structured scene representations. However, storing observations or high-dimensional semantic embeddings incurs growing storage costs. Meanwhile, structured representations support retrieval and semantic reasoning but do not explicitly evolve accumulated experience into environment-specific knowledge. To address these limitations, we propose Experience-Evolving Memory (EvoNav), a novel two-timescale memory framework. It organizes semantic observations, spatial relations, and task-feedback cues into sparse experience atoms. During online operation, experience atoms continually consolidate repeated observations and form dynamic links based on transitions. articles.title: Heave-Ho: Decentralized Long-Horizon Multi-Humanoid Collaboration
articles.summary: Collaboration promises to extend humanoid capabilities beyond what individual robots can achieve. However, realizing this potential requires coordinated whole-body interactions, coherent long-horizon planning, and precise synchronization across robots. We introduce Heave-Ho, a decentralized framework for long-horizon collaborative multi-humanoid loco-manipulation. At the low level, we develop a multi-agent post-training framework that adapts a humanoid foundation tracking model to physically coupled interactions between humanoids, enabling coordinated decentralized control from local observations alone. At the high level, we train a vision-language planner and design a speech-based leader-follower coordination mechanism to synchronize decentralized execution without network communication. Trained with two identical humanoids, our system scales to teams of up to ten robots and generalizes to heterogeneous teams without retraining. articles.title: ALERT: Extending Humanoid Motion Trackers with a General and Lightweight Human Avoidance Pipeline
articles.summary: Whole-body motion tracking has enabled humanoid dancing, athletic motions, and teleoperation, providing a foundation for capability demonstrations and manipulation data collection. However, existing tracking policies lack awareness of nearby humans and proactive avoidance capabilities, while motion substitution and local constraint-based corrections may compromise reference motion integrity and tracking continuity. We propose ALERT, a general lightweight pipeline for extending motion tracking to shared human-robot environments. Through lightweight adaptation, it integrates human perception and proactive avoidance into pretrained tracking policies, balancing avoidance demands with reference motion tracking while preserving existing motion capabilities. articles.title: From Temperature-Limited to Battery-Limited Legged Locomotion
articles.summary: On legged robots, sustained locomotion often ends in thermal shutdown rather than battery depletion: the heat of walking concentrates in a few joint motors, which overheat long before the battery is empty. We train thermally aware locomotion policies by reinforcement learning without ever observing temperature, and demonstrate this on a Unitree Go2 quadruped. Under a sustained gait, the temperatures the motors will settle at follow directly from the gait-averaged squared torques and joint speeds. articles.title: DailyBrick: Language-Guided Synthesis of Brick Assembly Instructions
articles.summary: Generating a LEGO model from a user request is more than a plausible 3D shape generation. LEGO models require physical support per brick, and each brick should be placed unblocked. Current methods address this issue by training an expert large language model. We reduce the problem of generating extremely long context on all brick connections to that of writing a program that builds LEGO models like a human, considering each intermediate step could be executed. We introduce DailyBrick , a multi-stage agentic system that produces a LEGO model together with a brick-by-brick assembly instruction for human building and robot assembly. We design a multi-stage harness with roles to help LLMs generate more effectively. A versioned construction SDK compiles multi-level decisions, from semantic subparts to individual bricks, into canonical operations. articles.title: DreamFAR: Real-Time and Long-Horizon Interaction with Diverse Objects
articles.summary: World models have shown great potential in serving as a simulator for robot manipulation. However, existing models are either fit to a single environment or lack ability to simulate long-horizon contact-rich events. We present DreamFAR, a world model whose dynamics model is trained from scratch on a large robot-native teleoperation dataset, with no internet-video pretraining. We present an architecture and learning recipe designed for training on robot-native data. DreamFAR is significantly smaller than the high-performance video generation models, yet shows better understanding of contact and causality, and runs 10 FPS on a commercial GPU. Experimentally, DreamFAR significantly outperforms existing models in predicting the long-horizon future. We further demonstrate various applications where DreamFAR can be used, including policy evaluation and mixed-data co-training. Project page: https://www.yimingdou.com/DreamFAR/

articles.title: HubEgo-100K: In-the-Wild Egocentric Video of Skilled Work for Robot Learning
articles.summary: Robot policies trained by imitation generalize poorly outside the environments and objects seen in training. Published data-scaling studies find that generalization grows with the diversity of training environments and objects rather than with more demonstrations per environment. Robot data is costly to collect across many environments, whereas egocentric human video can be recorded in the wild at scale; existing egocentric video, however, mostly shows daily-life activity and contains little skilled work in real workplaces. We present HubEgo-100K, a dataset built for diversity. This version of the paper covers the first release, v1.0: 10,124 hours of 1080p egocentric video with synchronized 100 Hz inertial (IMU) data from one head-mounted phone camera. articles.title: ALOHA Lightning: Learning Fast and Precise Manipulation
articles.summary: Learning from human demonstrations has enabled robots to acquire a wide range of manipulation skills, but learned policies typically execute far slower than ordinary humans. This speed gap is mainly due to lack of an interface for collecting demonstration data at high speed, and the difficulty in training policies that can robustly execute high-speed motions. In this paper, we present ALOHA Lightning (Flash ALOHA), a system for learning fast and precise robotic manipulation. Our system uses kinesthetic teaching to intuitively collect near-human-speed demonstrations on a backdrivable bimanual platform, yielding natural and fast trajectories. We also present a learning pipeline that enables smooth high-speed execution through test-time action smoothing and aligns the visual data distribution between data collection and deployment with masking. articles.title: From Human Videos to Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation Data: Confidence-Guided RL Refinement of Video Priors
articles.summary: Collecting demonstrations for bimanual dexterous manipulation is costly, motivating the use of human videos as a source of robot training data. However, uncertainty in video-derived motion estimates and differences between human and robot embodiments make direct motion transfer challenging. In this work, we introduce PriDex, a framework that transforms human-video Priors into executable robot Dexterous manipulation demonstrations through reinforcement learning in simulation. PriDex preserves task-relevant interaction structure while allowing embodiment-specific behavior to be regenerated for the robot. Human-object interactions provide affordance cues for selecting task-relevant, robot-specific grasps from geometry-based candidates. For motion refinement, object trajectories provide a task-level reference, while relative bimanual wrist trajectories offer complementary guidance for coordinated motion. articles.title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
articles.summary: Frontier Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in robot control, suggesting that broad pretraining provides knowledge valuable for physical action. Yet most Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies still rely on much smaller VLM backbones, leaving this potential largely untapped. We ask whether frontier-scale representations can provide a stronger foundation for robot learning. We introduce ScaleVLA, which connects a 552B DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash backbone to a trainable action DiT, and systematically compare VLMs from 2B to 552B under a shared training setup. We evaluate three fundamental capabilities of robot foundation models. In sample efficiency, just 10 demonstrations outperform a 2B backbone trained with 50 (87.8% vs. 85.6%). In generalization, LIBERO-PRO success reaches 45.1%, compared with at most 31.3% for smaller backbones. articles.title: Lazy-MOSAIC: Accelerating Skill-Centric Manipulation Planning with Learned Skill-Effect World Models
articles.summary: Long-horizon manipulation tasks require a robot to perform a sequence of physical interactions with its environment, typically combining several different skills. Planning such behaviors efficiently is challenging: given a library of parameterized skills, solutions lie in a vast hybrid space of skill sequences and their parameters, and evaluating each candidate skill's feasibility and effect with a high-fidelity world model such as a physics simulator is computationally expensive. MOSAIC, a recent skill-centric approach, lets the skills guide a non-sequential search toward the regions of this space where they are likely to succeed; however, it pays the full cost of simulation for every parameterized skill it considers. In this work, we introduce Lazy-MOSAIC, a lazy planning framework that instead searches over hypothesized skill outcomes. articles.title: Safe Physical Interaction of All-Electric Heavy-Duty Robotic Manipulators via Control Barrier Functions and Variable Impedance Control
articles.summary: All-electric heavy-duty robotic manipulators are increasingly expected to operate close to tunnel walls, equipment, and other structures while retaining the force capability required for large-payload tasks. Accurate motion control alone does not address the resulting safety and interaction requirements. This paper develops a safety-aware physical-interaction architecture that combines variable impedance control (VIC) with control barrier functions (CBFs) on top of an established virtual decomposition control (VDC) framework for electromechanical linear actuator (EMLA)-driven manipulators. VIC continuously adapts the task-space stiffness and damping according to predicted proximity and contact risk, whereas a joint-velocity CBF filter enforces Cartesian workspace boundaries and the physical stroke limits induced by the closed-chain lift and tilt mechanisms. articles.title: BoBDeLaN: Bounded-Bandwidth Context Adaptation for Deep Lagrangian Robot Control
articles.summary: Learned physics-based models provide structure for robot control, but uncertain payloads and unmodeled dynamics limit their predictive accuracy. Context-aware Deep Lagrangian Networks enable adaptation through a latent context inferred from measurement histories while retaining Lagrangian structure for each fixed context. However, this structure alone does not constrain sensitivity to measurement disturbances. We introduce BoBDeLaN, which combines a contracting, gain-bounded Recurrent Equilibrium Network context encoder with stable linear filtering to shape disturbance sensitivity across frequencies. articles.title: Cooperative Mobile Manipulation using Learned Dynamical Systems
articles.summary: Cooperative mobile manipulation requires robots to coordinate their motions while ensuring whole-body collision avoidance and preserving task-relevant behaviors. We propose CALDS (Cooperative Adaptation of Learned Dynamical Systems), a framework that enables mobile manipulators to adapt learned single-agent behaviors for coordinated execution. Building on individual dynamical systems (DSs) learned from demonstrations, CALDS enables cooperative adaptation through two key components: Cooperative Policy Selection, which identifies compatible combinations of learned policies, and Temporal Adaptation, which ensures collision-free cooperation while preserving the spatial structure and convergence properties of the original behaviors. articles.title: WinDEX: Metric 3D Hand Motion Reconstruction in the Wild for Dexterous Teleoperation and Policy Learning
articles.summary: Human manipulation data are widely used to train robots for human-like dexterity. However, low-cost, large-scale collection in the wild remains challenging. Existing methods remain limited in geometrically grounded metric-scale reconstruction, real-world generalization and inference speed. articles.title: ReuseMem: One Memory, Multiple Goals in Robot Manipulation
articles.summary: Robots that work alongside people should be able to use what they have seen when new requests arise. The same experience may later support identifying an object or returning it to its original location, although these uses were unknown during observation. ReuseMem learns to use one visual memory for multiple later manipulation goals. It records visual features independently of future goals, retrieves complementary evidence for each request, and combines it with the current scene through a lightweight action interface. Retrieval is supervised by how well candidate evidence supports expert-action prediction across different current states, linking memory selection to its use in manipulation. articles.title: ForceHarness: Turning Force into Action and Physics for Frozen Frontier Models
articles.summary: Frontier multimodal models can now control robots zero-shot from images, yet many manipulation tasks depend on contact forces that images cannot show. Second, a frozen model cannot interpret raw force streams, so force must be returned in a form the model can reason about. After calibrating hand force from a wrist sensor or joint torques alone, ForceHarness addresses the first challenge with self-terminating force primitives that regulate force on their own and return at a contact event. articles.title: Multi-CONDOR: Learning Multistable Motion Primitives from Demonstration
articles.summary: Dynamical-system-based motion policies provide a framework for learning reactive robot motions with stability and convergence properties. Many manipulation tasks, however, admit several distinct goals or a continuous set of acceptable outcomes, requiring motion primitives that preserve these alternatives. Accommodating both goal structures within a unified framework with continuous, autonomous dynamics remains an open challenge. We propose a CONDOR-based framework, multi-CONDOR, for learning motion primitives with either multiple discrete attractors or a continuous attracting goal contour. The approach combines imitation learning with losses that encourage agreement between the learned task dynamics and latent reference systems encoding the desired attraction structure. articles.title: WiTac: Wrist-Informed Tactile Representations for Contact-Rich Manipulation
articles.summary: Similar tactile contacts can call for different corrections depending on the configuration of the hand, object and target. Rather than supplying touch and wrist vision separately, fusing them before policy injection better grounds tactile features in visual context, yielding more accurate contact representations. Pretrained on nearly 300 hours of SharpaDex data, WiTac deeply fuses tactile signals with hand motion and wrist views into a comprehensive contact representation. articles.title: ROSE: A Shared Cross-Embodiment Facial-Motion Latent Space for Humanoid Robot Expression
articles.summary: Natural, coherent full-face dynamic expressions are central to making humanoid robots socially approachable, yet existing systems commonly realize only limited lip motion or scripted expressions. The limitation is both physical and algorithmic. A compact head leaves little room for densely packed, independently controllable actuation; meanwhile, learned systems often generate an avatar video, landmarks, or facial parameters and then infer actuator commands through visual retargeting. This render-and-invert path adds latency and artifacts, and it does not reliably transfer generated behavior to a physical robot. We present ROSE (RObot facial expression through Shared motion Embeddings), a framework that integrates biomimetic hardware, cross-embodiment motion representation learning, and multimodal motion generation. articles.title: TacBridge: Learning Unified Tactile Representations through Cross-Sensor Correspondence
articles.summary: Optical tactile sensors record tactile videos that capture local deformation and its temporal evolution during contact, supporting robot manipulation, force estimation, and tactile representation learning. This variability limits representation transfer and the joint use of multi-sensor data. articles.title: Driving the Style: Velocity-Conditioned Whole-Body Control from Motion Demonstrations
articles.summary: Achieving human-like behavior on humanoid robots has advanced rapidly by leveraging motion-capture demonstrations rather than hand-crafted cost functions. Adversarial imitation supplies a style signal that lets a policy fulfill a task while adhering to a desired style, but is difficult to transfer to hardware. articles.title: ACiT: Proprioceptive-Prior Action Chunking with Inverted Transformers
articles.summary: Visuomotor policies condition action prediction on visual and proprioceptive observations. articles.summary: Tactile sensing is essential for contact-rich manipulation, yet heterogeneous sensing mechanisms and observation formats hinder cross-hardware transfer. Specifically, we pair tactile observations from all sensors with wrench measurements, enabling shared physical supervision without requiring direct tactile-to-tactile pairing between sensors. articles.title: SG-ODOM: Event-Driven Proprioceptive State Estimation with Stability-Gated Contact Updates for Legged Robots
articles.summary: Reliable proprioceptive state estimation for legged robots fuses inertial sensing with kinematic sensing from leg encoders. Repeatedly applying kinematic corrections throughout the same contact phase can introduce redundant or unreliable information. Following physical touchdown, a stability gate accepts the contact for state estimation only after the foot reaches a sufficiently stable support condition. articles.summary: Teleoperated demonstrations are costly to collect and rarely reusable across end-effectors with different kinematics and action spaces. This burden grows in bimanual manipulation, where each end-effector pair may require new data. We present AsymEEF, a framework for executable cross-end-effector demonstration generation and unified bimanual policy learning. Given a small source dataset, AsymEEF transfers demonstrations to heterogeneous combinations of two-, three-, and five-fingered end-effectors without additional teleoperation. Kinematic teacher anchors provide geometric supervision, while sparse real-world X-Calib anchors correct discrepancies in grasp execution. articles.title: VoxSAOR: Semantic-Aware Occupancy Robustification via Aleatoric Uncertainty Modeling
articles.summary: Vision-based 3D occupancy prediction provides a dense semantic representation of scenes for autonomous driving and embodied perception, yet remains vulnerable to occlusion, depth ambiguity, and projection errors that induce spatially varying reliability in voxel features. Existing methods typically map voxel representations to semantic predictions without explicitly modeling such observation-induced feature variations. articles.title: Lift, See, Act: Hierarchical Robot Policy Pretraining with 3D Foundation Models
articles.summary: Robot policy pretraining based on human videos is crucial for improving the policy's generalization ability. One main challenge for this task is the lack of explicit action-relevant representations in such unlabeled data. Recent works tend to estimate 3D hand motion trajectories from videos using 3D foundation models (3D FMs). However, they keep solely the sparse trajectories as supervision, ignoring the rich, fine-grained information produced during the trajectory extraction process. To address this issue, we propose LSA, a hierarchical robot policy pretraining framework that includes three phases: Lift, See, and Act. articles.summary: Flow-based vision-language-action (VLA) models achieve strong performance in robotics through imitation learning, yet fine-tuning them with on-policy reinforcement learning (RL) is limited. articles.title: XMimic and XSoma: Learning Humanoid Motion Tracking and Locomotion in Under a Minute
articles.summary: We present XMimic and XSoma, which learn humanoid motion tracking and locomotion on rough terrain in under a minute of training. Both follow SuperMimic, which learns a world model of the robot and optimizes the policy with analytic gradients through short rollouts imagined in this model. Existing implementations of this method do not make use of larger GPUs, as every training iteration is a long chain of small GPU operations that run one after another. XMimic and XSoma therefore shorten this chain and run the steps of every iteration at the same time on up to four GPUs. We compile the complete training loop with JAX, including the MuJoCo Warp simulator. For locomotion, XSoma leaves only the dynamics of the robot to the world model and computes everything else exactly, including the terrain height under the feet. It learns with a horizon of one second and without a critic. On four H100 GPUs, XMimic learns to track all 40 LAFAN1 clips with the Unitree G1 in 0.86 minutes, 3.7 times faster

articles.title: NF-VLA: A Normalizing-Flow Baseline for Vision-Language-Action Learning
articles.summary: Autoregressive normalizing flows (NFs) provide a tractable density for learning and sampling continuous robot actions. We show that a single maximum-likelihood objective can train vision--language--action (VLA) policies competitive with leading methods on manipulation benchmarks. We present NF-VLA, which combines conditional autoregressive normalizing flows with score-based action refinement. Its deep--shallow architecture concentrates visual, language, and proprioceptive prefix conditioning in a high-capacity deep block, while unconditioned shallow blocks provide a shared invertible action transformation. The vision--language backbone and flow are jointly trained by exact maximum likelihood on Gaussian-smoothed action chunks. The same learned density supplies a single score-based correction at inference, refining generated actions to account for training-time smoothing without a separately trained denoiser.
